_meta.indication: TissueBlue (Brilliant Blue G Ophthalmic Solution) 0.025% is a disclosing agent indicated to selectively stain the internal limiting membrane (ILM).

pivotal_trials.trial_name: No sponsor-conducted pivotal trial; a 505(b)(2) application relying on published literature. Primary supporting evidence: Study #1, a systematic review/meta-analysis of BBG-assisted ILM peeling for macular hole.
pivotal_trials.phase: Not applicable — published literature (systematic review/meta-analysis and comparative case series), no applicant-sponsored phase trial.
pivotal_trials.design: Study #1: systematic review of MEDLINE, EMBASE and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials; outcome measures were primary closure rate and postoperative best-corrected visual acuity; all included studies retrospective except two randomized (Fu, Machida).
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with macular hole undergoing vitrectomy with internal limiting membrane (ILM) peeling.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary closure rate of the macular hole and postoperative best-corrected visual acuity.
pivotal_trials.n: The pivotal supporting evidence (Study #1 meta-analysis) pooled multiple published studies of BBG-assisted ILM peeling and does not report a single aggregate N. The individual comparative case series (Study #3) enrolled 50 eyes of 50 patients (26 women and 24 men) across BBG, trypan blue, and ICG groups.
pivotal_trials.result: The pivotal Study #1 meta-analysis author concluded there was no significant difference in anatomical outcome between dyes. In the supporting Study #3 comparative case series, macular hole closure was: Brilliant Blue 15 (100%), Trypan Blue 19 (95%), Indocyanine Green 13 (86%), P=0.480.

key_safety: Adverse reactions reported in procedures using TissueBlue have often been associated with the surgical procedure and include retinal complications (retinal break, tear, hemorrhage, and detachment) and cataracts.
target_moa: Brilliant Blue G forms a stable negatively charged complex with basic amino acid residues of proteins (mainly arginine and aromatic amino acids), selectively staining the ILM but not the epiretinal membrane or retina, making the transparent membrane easier to visualize for removal.

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee Meeting was held for this application; there were no issues thought to benefit from such a discussion.

orphan_indication.text: In 2012, OOPD granted orphan designation for Brilliant Blue G 0.025% Solution to selectively stain the internal limiting membrane (ILM); modified June 26, 2019 to "for use as an aid in ophthalmic surgery by selectively staining the internal limiting membrane."

summary.text: TissueBlue was approved as a 505(b)(2) NDA relying on published literature (no applicant-sponsored clinical studies), for an orphan-designated indication (granted 2012, modified June 26, 2019), with no advisory committee meeting held; the FD&C Act classifies it as a drug because of selective staining (chemical action within the body).
